::: {.why}
Every previous exercise let you stop, and the round does not, so the last practice of the week removes the pause and finds out what degrades.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Run a continuous 45-minute quoting session and report profit, inventory and adverse selection.
- Say which part of your decision quality degraded under continuous pressure.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [45 min]{.task-min} Run the full session with no pauses and no reference material, keeping a running commentary out loud. The commentary is the point: an interviewer is listening to how you decide, and doing it while under pressure is the skill that does not transfer from silent practice.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Review the recording rather than only the score: find the point where your reasoning became a heuristic instead of a calculation, and note what triggered it. It is usually an unexpected fill or a run of losses, and knowing your own trigger is worth more than the profit number.
:::
:::

::: {.deliverable}
A recorded 45-minute continuous session with profit, inventory and adverse selection reported, plus the identified degradation point.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
At what point in the session did your reasoning stop being a calculation, and what triggered it?
:::
